messages:
Anna L: Hey team — last night's nsys traces from the nightly perf job failed to upload and we missed the kernel stall that caused a latency regression. Can we spec how to automate trace collection in CI (nightly runs), store artifacts reliably, and make diffs for kernel timelines/hotspots?

Mike R: +1. We should capture deterministic slices using NVTX ranges so traces are comparable. Idea: wrap the critical inference window with NVTX push/pop and use nsys capture-range. Example command: 
```
nsys profile --output trace_${JOB_ID} --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \\n  --trace=cuda,osrt,cublas,cudnn \\n  python run_perf_workload.py --model gptq-8bit --seq-len 512 --nvtx-markers
```
This keeps trace size down and gives clean kernel boundaries.

Jess K: We also need artifact storage + retention rules. Proposal: upload gzip'd traces to s3://redwood-perf-traces/nightly/{commit}/{job_id}/trace.nsight.gz and keep an index.json per commit that lists run metadata (model, seed, config, kpis). Retain 90 days, then move to cold storage.

CI Bot: I've sketched a CI job template: perf-traces-nightly (runs on dedicated perf-runner). Steps: checkout pinned commit -> pull model artifacts -> run warmup + 3 measured runs -> collect NVTX-wrapped traces -> run small post-processing to extract per-kernel aggregates -> upload artifacts and index -> post link & summary to #eng-runtime.

Shane P: Note on perf-runner: isolate GPUs and increase host pinned-memory to avoid jitter. Also pin CPU governor and disable turbo for comparability. We'll need a label on the runner (perf=true) in the runner pool.

Mike R: For post-processing we can use nsight-convert/perfetto trace_processor to extract kernel timelines and durations. Minimal pipeline: 
```
# convert to perfetto json (if needed)
trace_processor_shell trace.pb --run_sql "SELECT name, SUM(dur)/1000 as us_total FROM slices GROUP BY name ORDER BY us_total DESC;" > kernel_agg.csv
```
Then publish kernel_agg.csv and a small JSON with top-10 kernels and their total us. Those are what the diff dashboard will compare.

Anna L: Good. For diffs we want: total inference latency, tokens/sec, top-10 kernels delta (us & %), and a flamegraph snapshot (perfetto UI link). Dashboard should show baseline vs current commit. Ideally clicking a kernel opens the raw trace in perfetto for that run.

Jess K: Perf artifacts will be large. Add two levels: full trace (gzipped, 7 days retention) and trimmed summary (csv/json + flamegraph svg) with 90 days retention. Also add metadata fields in index.json: run_id, commit_sha, model, seq_len, batch_size, gpu_type, runner_id, trace_size_bytes, kpi_latency_ms.

Mike R: To make traces diffable, standardize the workload harness: seed RNGs, deterministic batching, fixed token inputs. Also annotate each run with NVTX sections like: NVTX:SETUP, NVTX:WARMUP, NVTX:INFER_LOOP_START..END, NVTX:KV_CACHE_LOOKUP.

Shane P: Security note: redact any customer data before uploading. Use a transparent test corpus stored in infra artifacts bucket. Also ensure S3 permissions are the bucket-perf-ci role only.

Anna L: Implementation plan / milestones: 
- this week: add NVTX annotations and nsys wrapper in run_perf_workload.py (Mike)
- next week: CI job + upload script + index.json schema (Jess)
- then: post-processing scripts + trace -> kernel_agg extractor (Mike)
- dashboard prototype (Anna + Shane)

CI Bot: Action created: perf/TRACE-435 (automate nightly traces). Will run first job at 03:00 UTC tomorrow.

Jess K: SGTM. I'll provision the S3 path and lifecycle rules and create the perf-runner label.

Mike R: I'll add the trace conversion utilities and example notebook to generate kernel diff plots. Also will add a small sample trace (~10 MiB) to the repo for dev.

Anna L: One more: add a lightweight sanity check in CI that parses kernel_agg.csv and fails the job on >20% regression in top-3 kernels vs baseline (configurable). If the check fails, it should not block merges but open a perf-alert issue and notify #eng-runtime.

Shane P: We should avoid noisy alerts. Alert threshold and baseline commit should be in index.json. Also add a 'known_ignores' list for expected kernel variance (like cudnn autotune).

Mike R: I'll prototype the trace diff logic tomorrow and post results here. Anyone who wants to help with perfetto trace_processor SQL ping me.

Anna L: Thanks team. Let's keep the initial rollout narrow (one model, one seq_len) and iterate. :thumbsup:
